opti-1: Morning in the Everglades. Something hides in the grass.
opti-2: Look closer. Can you find what's hiding here?
opti-4: Pythons don't belong here. Scientists set cameras.
opti-5: Pythons climb, swim, and hide, and they eat native animals.
opti-6: With evidence, people write plans to protect animals like this rabbit.
opti-7: How do you choose a plan to save a park, and prove it will work?
25-02-welcome: Our film starts in a quiet marsh, with something hiding in the grass. First, inspect a strange specimen from the Everglades.
25-02-lesson: Today you're a park scientist. Build a proposal, test two trails, then watch a river come back.
25-02-check: Three quick questions. It's not graded. It's just for you, so give each one your best try.
25-02-assign: Time to write your own proposal. Name the threat, show your evidence, and tell us how you'll know it worked.
how-25-02-specimen: Press Inspect specimen. Move the magnifying lens over the specimen, then tap three things you notice.
how-25-02-compare: Put the boots under one tray and the water under the other: drag them, or tap one, then a tray. Press Run the test. Then swap.
how-25-02-wall: First, make a prediction. Then brush the glowing stop: drag across it (or tap it again and again) until the place shows.
how-25-02-det: Pick three threats, one at a time. Tap a clue, then name the threat. Predict a solution that fits, and watch it at work.
how-25-02-partc: Draw your solution in action in the park. Label the threat it stops, and one thing you will count or measure to check it.
